title: National Aviation Museum Act
full_text:
NATIONAL AVIATION MUSEUM ACT

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to contribute to the promotion of aviation culture and the development of the aviation industry by establishing the National Aviation Museum to discover, preserve, research, and exhibit the heritage of aviation culture and the aviation industry.

Article 2 (Legal personality)
The National Aviation Museum (hereinafter referred to as the "Museum") shall be a corporation.

Article 3 (Establishment)
(1) The Museum shall be established upon registration of its establishment at the location of its principal office.
(2) The following matters shall be registered under paragraph (1):
1. Objectives;
2. Name;
3. Principal office and affiliated institutions;
4. Names and addresses of officers;
5. Method of public notice.
(3) Except as provided in this Act, the provisions of the Civil Act concerning incorporated foundations shall apply mutatis mutandis to the registration of the Museum.

Article 4 (Articles of incorporation)
(1) The articles of incorporation of the Museum shall include the following:
1. Objectives;
2. Name;
3. Location of the principal office;
4. Business and its execution;
5. Property and accounting;
6. Organization and affiliated institutions;
7. Officers and employees;
8. Board of directors;
9. Amendments to the articles of incorporation;
10. Method of public notice.
(2) To amend the articles of incorporation of the Museum, a resolution shall be adopted by the board of directors with the affirmative votes of at least two thirds of all incumbent directors, and authorization shall be obtained from the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 5 (Projects)
(1) The Museum shall perform the following projects:
1. Formulation and implementation of the Museum's basic operational plan and medium- and long-term development plan;
2. Collection, preservation, management, and exhibition of museum materials (meaning materials related to aviation culture and the aviation industry prescribed by Presidential Decree; hereinafter the same shall apply);
3. Investigation and research of museum materials;
4. Education concerning museum materials;
5. Public relations concerning museum materials, and production and distribution of various publications related thereto;
6. Operation and management of affiliated institutions;
7. Domestic and international exchange and cooperation relating to museum materials;
8. Revenue-generating projects to secure operating funds within the scope of the purposes of establishing the Museum;
9. Activities incidental to the projects referred to in subparagraphs 1 through 8;
10. Other affairs related to aviation entrusted to the Museum by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.
(2) To conduct a revenue-generating project under paragraph (1) 8, the Museum shall obtain approval from the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport for each such project.

Article 6 (Officers)
(1) The Museum shall have one Director, two standing directors, not more than six non-standing directors, and one auditor as its officers.
(2) The auditor shall serve on a non-standing basis.
(3) The Director shall be appointed and dismissed by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport as prescribed by the articles of incorporation; the appointment and dismissal of standing directors, non-standing directors, and the auditor shall be governed by the articles of incorporation.

Article 7 (Terms of office of officers)
(1) The term of office of each officer shall be three years, and an officer may be reappointed for additional terms of one year each.
(2) The term of office of an officer appointed as a result of the resignation of another officer or for any similar reason shall commence anew.

Article 8 (Duties of officers)
(1) The Director shall represent the Museum, exercise general control over its affairs, and direct and supervise its employees.
(2) If the Director is unable to perform the duties of the office due to unavoidable circumstances, a standing director shall act on behalf of the Director in the order prescribed by the articles of incorporation; if the standing directors are also unable to perform those duties, an officer prescribed by the articles of incorporation shall act on behalf of the Director.
(3) Directors shall attend meetings of the board of directors and deliberate on matters submitted to the board.
(4) The auditor shall audit the accounting and execution of affairs of the Museum.

Article 9 (Grounds for disqualification of officers)
(1) None of the following persons may become an officer of the Museum:
1. A person who falls under any of the subparagraphs of Article 33 of the State Public Officials Act;
2. A person for whom three years have not passed since the date of dismissal under Article 22 (1), Article 35 (2) or (3), Article 36 (2), or Article 48 (4) or (8) of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions.
(2) If an officer comes to fall under any of the subparagraphs of paragraph (1), or is found to have fallen thereunder at the time of appointment, the officer shall automatically retire from office.
(3) Acts in which an officer who retires under paragraph (2) participated before retirement shall remain valid.

Article 10 (Board of directors)
(1) The Museum shall have a board of directors to deliberate on and resolve important matters of the Museum.
(2) The board of directors shall consist of directors, including its chairperson.
(3) The Director shall serve as the chairperson of the board of directors. If the chairperson is unable to perform the duties of the office due to unavoidable circumstances, a standing director shall act on behalf of the chairperson in the order prescribed by the articles of incorporation; if the standing directors are also unable to perform those duties, a person elected from among the non-standing directors shall act on behalf of the chairperson.
(4) The chairperson of the board of directors may convene a meeting of the board when the chairperson deems it necessary: Provided, That the chairperson shall convene a meeting upon a request by at least one third of all incumbent directors or upon a request by the auditor to report audit findings concerning illegal or improper matters.
(5) The board of directors shall adopt resolutions with the affirmative votes of a majority of all incumbent directors.
(6) The auditor may attend a meeting of the board of directors and express opinions when necessary in connection with the auditor's duties.

Article 11 (Financial resources)
(1) Expenses necessary for the projects and operation of the Museum shall be financed by the following resources:
1. Contributions and donations from the State or persons other than the State;
2. Borrowings under Article 13;
3. Revenue generated from the operation of the Museum;
4. Other revenue.
(2) The State may contribute funds necessary for the projects and operation of the Museum within its budget.
(3) An individual, corporation, or organization may contribute or donate money or other property to the Museum to support the performance of the Museum's affairs.
(4) Matters concerning procedures for receiving donated money and goods under paragraph (3) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 12 (Business year and business plan)
(1) The business year of the Museum shall coincide with the fiscal year of the Government.
(2) As prescribed by Presidential Decree, the Director shall prepare and submit a business plan and budget before the commencement of each business year and obtain approval from the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport. The same shall apply to any amendment thereto.
(3) As prescribed by Presidential Decree, the Director shall report to the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, within two months after the end of each fiscal year, a report on the Museum's business performance for that fiscal year and a statement of settlement of revenue and expenditure that has been audited by a certified public accountant (including an accounting corporation under Article 23 of the Certified Public Accountant Act) and approved by resolution of the board of directors.

Article 13 (Borrowings)
The Museum may borrow funds, when necessary for its operation, with approval from the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 14 (Supporters' association)
(1) The Museum may establish a supporters' association composed of members who provide support necessary for its smooth operation.
(2) The supporters' association may receive contributions from its members or collect goods needed by the Museum.
(3) The supporters' association shall transfer contributions received or goods collected under paragraph (2) to the Museum in accordance with the requirements prescribed by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.
(4) Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the supporters' association shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 15 (Entrustment and management of museum materials)
(1) For the specialized preservation and research of State-owned museum materials managed by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport at the time of the establishment of the Museum, the State may entrust their management to the Museum notwithstanding the Commodity Management Act.
(2) Officers and employees engaged in managing museum materials owned by the Museum or entrusted by the State under paragraph (1) shall perform their duties with the due care of a prudent manager, in addition to complying with statutes and relevant regulations concerning the management of museum materials.

Article 16 (Requests for provision of materials)
The Director may request relevant administrative agencies, educational institutions, research organizations, or other related persons to permit inspection, copying, lending, entrusted exhibition, or similar use of materials related to aviation culture and the aviation industry.

Article 17 (Requests for dispatch of public officials)
(1) If particularly necessary for performing the Museum's affairs, the Director may, with approval from the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, request the head of a relevant administrative agency or educational institution to dispatch affiliated public officials or other personnel.
(2) The head of a relevant administrative agency or educational institution requested to dispatch public officials or other personnel under paragraph (1) may dispatch employees belonging to that agency or institution to the Museum.

Article 18 (Supervision)
(1) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall guide and supervise the Museum and may make recommendations or issue orders concerning its projects when the Minister deems it necessary.
(2) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall evaluate the operation of the Museum in accordance with the standards and procedures prescribed by Presidential Decree and take necessary measures based on the results.
(3) When the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport deems it necessary, the Minister may require the Museum to report matters concerning its affairs, accounting, and property or may inspect such matters.

Article 19 (Preservation of surrounding landscape)
When granting a building permit under Article 11 of the Building Act for an area surrounding the Museum within the scope prescribed by ordinance, the head of a local government shall take appropriate measures to preserve the surrounding landscape.

Article 20 (Duty to maintain confidentiality)
No current or former officer or employee of the Museum shall divulge secrets learned in the course of performing official duties or use such secrets to acquire property or pecuniary benefits.

Article 21 (Prohibition of use of similar names)
No person other than the National Aviation Museum established under this Act shall use the name "National Aviation Museum" or any similar name.

Article 22 (Application mutatis mutandis)
Except as provided in this Act, the provisions of the Civil Act concerning incorporated foundations shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Museum.

Article 23 (Deemed status as public officials for purposes of penalties)
Officers and employees of the Museum shall be deemed public officials for the purposes of applying Articles 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act.

Article 24 (Penalties)
A person who divulges a secret learned in the course of performing official duties or uses such a secret to acquire property or pecuniary benefits, in violation of Article 20, shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than two years or by a fine not exceeding 20 million won.

Article 25 (Administrative fines)
(1) A person who uses the name "National Aviation Museum" or any similar name in violation of Article 21 shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding five million won.
(2) Administrative fines under paragraph (1) shall be imposed and collected by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

ADDENDA <Act No. 16490, August 20, 2019>

Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Act shall enter into force three months after the date of its promulgation: Provided, That Articles 2 and 7 of these Addenda shall enter into force on the date of promulgation.

Article 2 (Preparations for establishment)
(1) Within two months from the date of promulgation of this Act, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall establish the Committee for Establishment of the National Aviation Museum (hereinafter referred to as the "Establishment Committee"), consisting of not more than five establishment committee members, to handle affairs concerning the establishment of the Museum and the selection of directors and an auditor at the time of its establishment. In such cases, the chairperson and committee members shall be appointed or commissioned by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.
(2) The Establishment Committee shall prepare the articles of incorporation of the Museum and obtain authorization from the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.
(3) The Director of the Museum at the time of its establishment shall be appointed by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.
(4) Upon obtaining authorization under paragraph (2), the Establishment Committee shall, without delay, jointly register the establishment of the Museum under the names of its members and then hand over its affairs to the Director.
(5) Upon completion of the handover of affairs under paragraph (4), the Establishment Committee shall be deemed dissolved and the establishment committee members shall be deemed released from their appointments or commissions.
(6) Until the Museum is established, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall bear expenses incurred in establishing the Museum.
(7) If necessary for performing affairs relating to the establishment of the Museum, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may request the dispatch of officers, employees, or other personnel of relevant agencies or organizations.

[Effective date: August 20, 2019] Article 2

Article 3 (Transfer of commodities without compensation)
The State may transfer without compensation to the Museum State-owned commodities (excluding museum materials) managed by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (limited to the operation of the National Aviation Museum) at the time this Act enters into force, notwithstanding the Commodity Management Act. In such cases, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall hear the Director's opinion on whether the relevant commodities are needed and consult in advance with the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 4 (Succession to rights and obligations)
The Museum established under this Act shall comprehensively succeed to the rights and obligations belonging to the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (limited to the operation of the National Aviation Museum) as at the time this Act enters into force.

Article 5 (Budget at the time of establishment)
(1) Until the budget of the Museum established under this Act is finalized at the time of its establishment, the Museum may execute the budget previously allocated to the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (limited to the operation of the National Aviation Museum) according to the former practice.
(2) When the budget of the Museum is established, expenses executed under paragraph (1) shall be deemed to have been executed under that budget.

Article 6 (Special cases concerning appointment of employees)
(1) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall classify public officials under the Minister's jurisdiction who are engaged in affairs concerning the establishment of the Museum as at the time this Act enters into force into those who wish to be appointed as employees of the incorporated Museum and those who do not, according to their respective wishes.
(2) A person who wishes to be appointed as an employee of the Museum under paragraph (1) shall be deemed to have retired from public office and to have been appointed as an employee of the Museum when the corporation is established.
(3) Matters concerning the affiliation, job security, service relationships, and related matters of public officials who do not wish to be appointed as employees of the Museum under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(4) The retirement age of a person who retires from public office and is appointed as an employee of the Museum under paragraph (2) shall be the retirement age prescribed by the State Public Officials Act for the grade applicable to that person at the time of retirement from public office: Provided, That where the retirement age for an employee of the Museum is higher than that prescribed by the State Public Officials Act, the retirement age for employees of the Museum shall apply.

Article 7 (Transitional measures concerning budget formulation)
The Establishment Committee may prepare the budget of the Museum for the first business year commencing after the establishment of the Museum.

[Effective date: August 20, 2019] Article 7
